Follow the process step by step.
1. Sync Time
2. Exam Configuration
3. System Configuration
4. Boot the Client Systems
1- Sync Time
This is the first and important step. Whenever you log in to the Netboot Server
for the first time, you must update the date and time.
In the left-side menu panel, scroll to the bottom and click on “Time & Date”,
after clicking the current date and time will appear on the right side of the
screen. You will also see a red “Update” button.
Now follow these steps:
 First, set the Time Zone to “Asia/Kolkata.”
 Click the Update button, a confirmation popup will appear.
 Click Update again to confirm.
Note: - Make sure the Date and Time on your Windows machine (where
you are configuring netboot) are correct; otherwise, Netboot will not sync
properly.

2- Exam configurations
Navigate to the "Exam configurations" tab from the left-side menu. Under
"Exam Configuration", you will find the following options:
Exam active status
 By default, this is set to Inactive. Keep it as Inactive for now. We
will change this setting later.
Exam server IP
 Enter the Main Server IP address in the input box.
After entering the required details, click the "Update Configurations"
button to save the settings.
3- System Configuration
From the Left-Panel menu, click on “System Configurations” You will now
see the System Configurations section.
3.2- System Information:
System IP: Enter the IP address of your Netboot Server. Example:
192.168.2.1 Make sure you enter the correct IP address here.
System Subnet: Keep it /24 always, unless you are instructed by Master
Control or Tech Support.
DHCP Settings
DHCP Start IP: Enter the first IP in the DHCP range.
Example: 192.168.2.10
DHCP End IP: Enter the last IP to assign in the range.
Example: 192.168.2.250
Important: Do not include the Netboot Server, Main & Backup
Exam Server IP in this range. Keep them outside of the range to avoid
conflicts. IP for Registration Desk – You can use 192.168.2.2 to
192.168.2.9
Custom gateway IP
By default, this option is disabled. If you are not using a Sonic firewall, keep
this option Disabled. No changes are required. If you are using a Sonic firewall,
then enable this option and Follow the Steps:
 Click on the Enable option.
 Enter the IP address of the Sonic Firewall X0 Port IP in the field.
Note: - Make sure that this IP address is outside the DHCP range, Example:-
192.168.2.254
3.3- Node Behaviour Settings
Scroll down to configure how nodes (client systems) behave when they boot:
Node Registration:
Enable this to allow new clients (Nodes) to register with the Netboot Server
during their first boot.
Enabled – Clients can register.
 Keep Node Registration Enabled for Configuration
day.
Confirm and Apply Network Configuration
Click on the Update button to proceed. Once you clicked on the Update button.
A confirmation popup will appear like this:
First, click the Red “Update” button to save the settings. Then, click the Yellow
“Apply Network Configurations” button.
1- Update
2- Apply Network Configuration
Most Important-
Note:-
Once you click “Apply Network Configurations,” Netboot Server will restart its
network services. During this time, the server may temporarily go offline and might
not respond to ping. Wait patiently — do not interrupt the process. Once the server
is reachable again (ping is successful), you can continue with the remaining setup.
Use these buttons in the same sequence only, otherwise the
settings will not be saved.
